comment: Redirects from the retired Sphinx docs on pika.readthedocs.io to the MkDocs
site on pika.github.io/pika. Pushed by utils/push_rtd_redirects.py; see
RELEASE.md for the procedure. Tracked by gh-1620.
`from_url` carries no version prefix because these are page redirects,
which RTD applies across every version of the project: one rule covers
/en/stable/intro.html, /en/latest/intro.html and /en/1.3.2/intro.html.
Enumerating /en/stable/ paths instead would need one exact rule per
version and would miss the older versions search engines still index.
`to_url` carries `latest/` because the new site is versioned by mike and
has no unversioned page paths: /pika/intro/ is a 404, /pika/latest/intro/
is not. The site root is the deliberate exception, since /pika/ serves a
redirect that follows the `latest` alias and so survives an alias change.
Directory roots need their own rules. Sphinx serves /en/stable/ and
/en/stable/modules/ as directory indexes, and a rule on /index.html does
not match /. Those three were serving the retired docs at 200 while every
explicit .html path already redirected, and /en/stable/ is where the bare
readthedocs.io domain sends its visitors.
The last rule is the catch-all, and it is an `exact` redirect with a `*`
wildcard rather than a page redirect. RTD removed its `prefix` type and
says so in the API error: "Prefix redirects have been removed. Please use
an exact redirect /prefix/* instead." Its target is fixed rather than a
:splat passthrough, because the two sites do not share a URL shape: the
old paths end in .html and the new ones are directories, so passing the
tail through would 404 on every page. RTD appends new rules to the end of
the list, so the catch-all sits at the highest position and the specific
rules above it win; verified by checking that faq.html still reaches
latest/faq/ while an unmapped path reaches the docs home.
